# Potential gains and brain activity

Does increasing potential monetary gain produce a greater fMRI response in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) in the NARPS equal-indifference group?

Test the hypothesis that this response increases with potential gain.
Participants performed a mixed-gambles task, deciding whether to accept gambles with possible gains and losses.
In this group, the range of potential gains was twice the range of potential losses.

Investigate the question at the group-analysis stage using the supplied 54 participant gain-effect maps and metadata.
Preprocessing and individual modeling are fixed inputs, described in `upstream-methods.md`; do not repeat them or download time-series scans.
Choose scientifically defensible group models, quality checks, software and visualizations.
Account for what the supplied effect estimates measure and the limits of their upstream model.
Use whole-brain correction for multiple comparisons when evaluating support for the hypothesis, as required by the original study; justify how you identify vmPFC.

Produce a concise scientific report with informative figures and the code and results supporting your conclusions.
Explain uncertainty, exclusions and limitations, including what a lack of support would mean.
Prior teams' answers are not ground truth or a required result.

Source: [NARPS original analysis instructions, Hypothesis 1](https://www.narps.info/files/narps_instructions_for_analysis_teams.pdf).

Common execution resources

Use the root Pixi environment; add dependencies as needed. Keep the working `pixi.lock` ignored. Retain the exact final validated lock as ordinary Git on a separate `codex/env-<run>` branch, one commit above the final task commit; return to the task branch before finishing and report both commit IDs. Publishing your assigned task branch, its environment snapshot and annex artifacts through the configured remotes is authorized. Keep analysis outputs under `results/` in this experiment repository. For substantive analyses, capture complete command metadata, stdout/stderr, resource usage and run summaries with duct under `logs/`. Retain failed attempts and annex large outputs/logs.
Keep task-specific installations local to this experiment repository; do not change shared user configuration.

Use the supplied, pinned STAMPED skills to complete this study: start with do-full-research-loop and apply the related guidance where appropriate.

I’ll follow the supplied research-loop workflow, first checking its instructions and the repository’s existing protocol, inputs, and execution conventions. I’ll keep the analysis at the group stage and use the provided participant maps and metadata.

*** Add File: protocol.md
+# Group analysis protocol
+
+## Question and target
+
+Test whether the group mean gain-effect estimate is positive in the equal-indifference cohort, and whether any whole-brain-corrected positive effect overlaps an independently specified vmPFC region. The sampling unit is participant (54 participants); the estimand is the mean of AO86's participant-level gain contrast estimates over this cohort. It is not a currency-unit slope or a causal effect of changing gain.
+
+## Fixed inputs and exclusions
+
+Use all 54 participant maps enumerated in `input/sources.json`, joined one-to-one to `input/participants.tsv` by participant ID. Verify map count, checksums, dimensions, affine, finite values and the common nonzero support. No participants are excluded unless an input is missing, corrupt, nonfinite or spatially incompatible; report any such exclusion by ID and reason. The cohort table is the complete equal-indifference group, so demographic covariates are not needed for this one-sample question.
+
+## Primary inference
+
+At each voxel in the intersection of participant nonzero support, calculate a one-sample t statistic against zero and test the prespecified positive direction. Control family-wise error across all tested voxels with a one-sided maximum-t sign-flip permutation test (5,000 random participant-level sign assignments, seed 20261016). This requires exchangeability of signs under the null and symmetric participant errors; the small Monte Carlo p-value resolution is 1/5,001. A vmPFC claim requires a positive voxel passing whole-brain FWE p < .05 inside the vmPFC mask. The mask is the union of Harvard-Oxford cortical atlas 2-mm, 25%-threshold maximum-probability labels `Frontal Medial Cortex`, `Subcallosal Cortex`, `Paracingulate Gyrus`, and `Frontal Orbital Cortex`, nearest-neighbor resampled to the supplied maps. This is an explicit, broad anatomical operationalization, not a universally agreed boundary.
+
+Report the voxelwise effect mean, t, uncorrected p, maximum-t FWE p, and coordinates at the strongest positive voxel. Also report a descriptive participant-level vmPFC mean and t-based 95% CI, and a leave-one-participant-out range for that mean. The atlas ROI summary is descriptive and cannot establish support without the whole-brain-corrected criterion.
+
+## Validity and limits
+
+Input checksums and participant joins must match the committed source manifest. Check common spatial geometry, finite values, sample sizes, and the computed mask/ROI sizes. Display the effect distribution and corrected whole-brain result. The maps are first-level contrast parameter estimates from AO86, not standardized statistics; their regressor was centered and variance-normalized before HRF convolution, so coefficients are not per-unit monetary effects. Separate gain/loss models mean gain effects are conditional on that upstream choice. No participant variance maps or executable upstream workflow are supplied, preventing a first-level precision-weighted mixed-effects analysis. A null corrected result means insufficient evidence at this sample and correction threshold; it does not establish no vmPFC response or equivalence to zero.
+
+## Stopping rule
+
+Stop if checksums fail, maps cannot be consistently registered, or the vmPFC mask has no overlap with the tested support. Do not change the model or threshold in response to observed significance. Any method change must be recorded as a separately named analysis.
*** Add File: code/analyze.py
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""One-sample group inference for supplied NARPS AO86 gain contrast maps."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import platform
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import matplotlib
+matplotlib.use("Agg")
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import nibabel as nib
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+from nilearn import datasets, image, plotting
+from scipy.stats import t as t_dist
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+MANIFEST = ROOT / "input/sources.json"
+PARTICIPANTS = ROOT / "input/participants.tsv"
+OUT = ROOT / "results"
+ATLAS_PATH = ROOT / "input/reference/HarvardOxford-cort-maxprob-thr25-2mm.nii.gz"
+N_PERM = 5000
+SEED = 20261016
+
+
+def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as f:
+        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            h.update(block)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def get_atlas():
+    if not ATLAS_PATH.exists():
+        atlas = datasets.fetch_atlas_harvard_oxford("cort-maxprob-thr25-2mm")
+        ATLAS_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        nib.save(atlas.maps, ATLAS_PATH)
+    return nib.load(ATLAS_PATH)
+
+
+def load_inputs(limit: int | None = None):
+    manifest = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text())
+    cohort = pd.read_csv(PARTICIPANTS, sep="\t")
+    if cohort.participant_id.duplicated().any():
+        raise ValueError("Duplicate participant_id in cohort table")
+    source_files = manifest["files"]
+    entries = [(p, m) for p, m in source_files.items() if p.endswith(".nii.gz")]
+    entries.sort(key=lambda item: item[1]["participant_id"])
+    if limit:
+        entries = entries[:limit]
+    ids = [m["participant_id"] for _, m in entries]
+    if limit is None and (len(entries) != 54 or set(ids) != set(cohort.participant_id)):
+        raise ValueError("Input maps do not match all 54 cohort participants")
+    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)) or not set(ids) <= set(cohort.participant_id):
+        raise ValueError("Map IDs are duplicated or absent from participant table")
+    arrays, img0, checkrows = [], None, []
+    for rel, meta in entries:
+        path = ROOT / rel
+        if not path.is_file():
+            raise FileNotFoundError(path)
+        digest = sha256(path)
+        if digest != meta["sha256"]:
+            raise ValueError(f"Checksum mismatch: {rel}")
+        img = nib.load(path)
+        arr = img.get_fdata(dtype=np.float32)
+        if img0 is None:
+            img0 = img
+        if arr.shape != img0.shape or not np.allclose(img.affine, img0.affine, atol=1e-5):
+            raise ValueError(f"Spatial shape/affine mismatch: {rel}")
+        if not np.isfinite(arr).all():
+            raise ValueError(f"Nonfinite values: {rel}")
+        arrays.append(arr)
+        checkrows.append({"participant_id": meta["participant_id"], "path": rel,
+                          "sha256": digest, "shape": arr.shape,
+                          "min": float(arr.min()), "max": float(arr.max())})
+    return np.stack(arrays), img0, ids, checkrows
+
+
+def tstat(values):
+    n = values.shape[0]
+    mean = values.mean(axis=0)
+    sd = values.std(axis=0, ddof=1)
+    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
+        stat = mean / (sd / np.sqrt(n))
+    return mean, np.nan_to_num(stat, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
+
+
+def perm_max_t(voxels, observed, n_perm=N_PERM, seed=SEED, chunk=8192):
+    """One-sided max-t sign flip with invariant sum of squares, chunked over voxels."""
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    signs = rng.choice(np.array([-1.0, 1.0]), size=(n_perm, voxels.shape[0]))
+    n = voxels.shape[0]
+    maxima = np.full(n_perm, -np.inf)
+    for start in range(0, voxels.shape[1], chunk):
+        x = voxels[:, start:start + chunk]
+        sums = signs @ x
+        means = sums / n
+        centered_ss = np.maximum(np.sum(x * x, axis=0)[None, :] - n * means * means, 1e-30)
+        stats = means / np.sqrt(centered_ss / (n - 1) / n)
+        maxima = np.maximum(maxima, stats.max(axis=1))
+    fwe = (1 + (maxima[:, None] >= observed[None, :]).sum(axis=0)) / (n_perm + 1)
+    return fwe, maxima
+
+
+def save_map(data, ref, path, dtype=np.float32):
+    img = nib.Nifti1Image(np.asarray(data, dtype=dtype), ref.affine, ref.header)
+    nib.save(img, path)
+
+
+def pilot():
+    data, ref, ids, rows = load_inputs(limit=3)
+    support = np.all(np.isfinite(data), axis=0) & np.any(data != 0, axis=0)
+    if not support.any():
+        raise ValueError("Pilot common nonzero support is empty")
+    mean, stat = tstat(data[:, support])
+    print(json.dumps({"mode": "pilot", "participants": ids, "shape": data.shape,
+                      "support_voxels": int(support.sum()), "mean_range": [float(mean.min()), float(mean.max())],
+                      "t_range": [float(stat.min()), float(stat.max())],
+                      "checksum_verified": len(rows)}, indent=2))
+
+
+def run():
+    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    data, ref, ids, input_rows = load_inputs()
+    n = len(ids)
+    support = np.all(np.isfinite(data), axis=0) & np.all(data != 0, axis=0)
+    if not support.any():
+        raise ValueError("Common nonzero support is empty")
+    flat = data[:, support].astype(np.float64)
+    mean, observed = tstat(flat)
+    p_unc = t_dist.sf(observed, n - 1)
+    p_fwe, null_maxima = perm_max_t(flat, observed)
+
+    atlas_img = get_atlas()
+    atlas_res = image.resample_to_img(atlas_img, ref, interpolation="nearest")
+    atlas_arr = atlas_res.get_fdata().astype(int)
+    labels = list(datasets.fetch_atlas_harvard_oxford("cort-maxprob-thr25-2mm").labels)
+    roi_labels = ["Frontal Medial Cortex", "Subcallosal Cortex", "Paracingulate Gyrus", "Frontal Orbital Cortex"]
+    roi_ids = [labels.index(name) for name in roi_labels]
+    roi = np.isin(atlas_arr, roi_ids)
+    roi_support = roi & support
+    if not roi_support.any():
+        raise ValueError("vmPFC atlas ROI does not overlap common tested support")
+    # Use 0.05 FWE threshold as the sole confirmatory decision rule.
+    fwe_vol = np.zeros(ref.shape, dtype=np.float32)
+    pvol = np.ones(ref.shape, dtype=np.float32)
+    meanvol = np.zeros(ref.shape, dtype=np.float32)
+    tvol = np.zeros(ref.shape, dtype=np.float32)
+    fwe_vol[support] = p_fwe
+    pvol[support] = p_unc
+    meanvol[support] = mean
+    tvol[support] = observed
+    sig = support & (fwe_vol < .05) & (tvol > 0)
+    roi_sig = sig & roi
+    p_index = int(np.argmax(np.where(roi_support, np.where(sig, tvol, -np.inf), -np.inf))) if roi_sig.any() else None
+    peak_index = int(np.argmax(tvol))
+    flat_indices = np.flatnonzero(support)
+    def peak_record(k):
+        ijk = np.unravel_index(int(flat_indices[k]), ref.shape)
+        xyz = nib.affines.apply_affine(ref.affine, ijk)
+        return {"ijk": [int(x) for x in ijk], "mni_xyz_mm": [round(float(x), 1) for x in xyz],
+                "mean_effect": float(mean[k]), "t": float(observed[k]), "p_uncorrected": float(p_unc[k]),
+                "p_fwe_max_t": float(p_fwe[k])}
+    roi_values = data[:, roi_support].mean(axis=1)
+    roi_mean = float(roi_values.mean())
+    roi_se = float(roi_values.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(n))
+    roi_ci = [roi_mean - t_dist.ppf(.975, n - 1) * roi_se,
+              roi_mean + t_dist.ppf(.975, n - 1) * roi_se]
+    loo = [(roi_values.sum() - x) / (n - 1) for x in roi_values]
+    table = pd.DataFrame({"participant_id": ids, "vmPFC_mean_effect": roi_values})
+    table.to_csv(OUT / "participant-vmpfc-effects.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
+    pd.DataFrame(input_rows).drop(columns="shape").to_csv(OUT / "input-checksums.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
+    save_map(meanvol, ref, OUT / "group-mean-effect.nii.gz")
+    save_map(tvol, ref, OUT / "group-t.nii.gz")
+    save_map(fwe_vol, ref, OUT / "group-fwe-p.nii.gz")
+    save_map(roi.astype(np.uint8), ref, OUT / "vmpfc-mask.nii.gz", dtype=np.uint8)
+    save_map(sig.astype(np.uint8), ref, OUT / "wholebrain-fwe-significant.nii.gz", dtype=np.uint8)
+
+    summary = {
+        "analysis": "one-sample positive group mean; maximum-t sign-flip permutation FWE",
+        "n": n, "participant_ids": ids, "excluded": [], "voxel_count": int(support.sum()),
+        "roi_voxels_in_support": int(roi_support.sum()), "roi_labels": roi_labels,
+        "atlas": "Harvard-Oxford cortical max-probability 25%, 2 mm; nearest-neighbor resampled to input space",
+        "permutations": N_PERM, "seed": SEED, "monte_carlo_min_p": 1/(N_PERM+1),
+        "voxelwise_fwe_alpha": .05, "significant_positive_voxels_whole_brain": int(sig.sum()),
+        "significant_positive_voxels_vmpfc": int(roi_sig.sum()), "positive_vmpfc_support": bool(roi_sig.any()),
+        "strongest_positive_voxel": peak_record(peak_index),
+        "strongest_positive_vmpfc_fwe_voxel": peak_record(int(np.where(support)[0].tolist().index(p_index))) if p_index is not None else None,
+        "vmpfc_participant_mean": roi_mean, "vmpfc_t_ci95": [float(x) for x in roi_ci],
+        "vmpfc_leave_one_out_mean_range": [float(min(loo)), float(max(loo))],
+        "vmpfc_participant_sd": float(roi_values.std(ddof=1)),
+        "null_max_t_quantiles": {str(q): float(np.quantile(null_maxima, q)) for q in [.5, .95, .99]},
+        "input_manifest_sha256": sha256(MANIFEST), "participants_tsv_sha256": sha256(PARTICIPANTS),
+        "python": sys.version, "platform": platform.platform(),
+    }
+    (OUT / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + "\n")
+    pd.DataFrame({"null_max_t": null_maxima}).to_csv(OUT / "permutation-max-t.tsv.gz", sep="\t", index=False, compression="gzip")
+    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
+
+    # Descriptive participant spread with estimate and interval.
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5), constrained_layout=True)
+    jitter = np.random.default_rng(SEED).normal(0, .045, n)
+    ax.scatter(1 + jitter, roi_values, s=25, alpha=.7, color="#34495e", edgecolor="white", linewidth=.35)
+    ax.errorbar(1.18, roi_mean, yerr=[[roi_mean - roi_ci[0]], [roi_ci[1] - roi_mean]], fmt="D",
+                color="#c0392b", capsize=4, label="Mean and 95% t interval")
+    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=.8, linestyle="--")
+    ax.set(xlim=(.72, 1.48), xticks=[], ylabel="Participant mean gain-effect estimate",
+           title="vmPFC atlas-mask estimates (descriptive; n=54)")
+    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="best")
+    fig.savefig(OUT / "vmpfc-participant-estimates.png", dpi=180)
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+    # Display the t map with only whole-brain FWE-significant voxels retained.
+    display_stat = np.where(sig, tvol, 0)
+    stat_img = nib.Nifti1Image(display_stat, ref.affine, ref.header)
+    if sig.any():
+        display = plotting.plot_stat_map(stat_img, display_mode="ortho", cut_coords=(0, 35, -10),
+                                         threshold=0, cmap="magma", colorbar=True,
+                                         title="Positive effects surviving whole-brain max-t FWE p < .05")
+    else:
+        display = plotting.plot_stat_map(nib.Nifti1Image(tvol, ref.affine, ref.header),
+                                         display_mode="ortho", cut_coords=(0, 35, -10),
+                                         threshold=0, cmap="magma", colorbar=True,
+                                         title="Group t map (no positive voxels survive whole-brain FWE p < .05)")
+    display.savefig(OUT / "wholebrain-fwe-map.png", dpi=180)
+    display.close()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--pilot", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    pilot() if args.pilot else run()
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

+
+The vmPFC operationalization uses labels in the Harvard-Oxford cortical atlas, `cort-maxprob-thr25-2mm`, distributed by FSL and fetched with Nilearn's `fetch_atlas_harvard_oxford`. *** Add File: results/report.md
+# Potential gain effects in the NARPS equal-indifference group
+
+## Question and analysis
+
+We tested whether gain-related activity was positive in vmPFC in the 54-person equal-indifference group. The participant was the unit of analysis. We fit a one-sample group test of the supplied participant contrast estimates against zero, in the prespecified positive direction. Voxelwise family-wise error was controlled across the common participant support (198,029 voxels) with 5,000 participant-level sign flips and a maximum-t statistic (seed 20261016; minimum attainable Monte Carlo p = 0.00020).
+
+We operationalized vmPFC as the union of Harvard-Oxford cortical atlas labels Frontal Medial Cortex, Subcallosal Cortex, Paracingulate Gyrus, and Frontal Orbital Cortex. This broad, prespecified mask contributed 6,174 tested voxels after nearest-neighbor resampling. Since vmPFC has no single agreed anatomical boundary, the mask is an explicit working definition. Support required a positive voxel inside it to pass the same whole-brain FWE p < .05 threshold; the ROI average below is descriptive and does not replace that criterion.
+
+## Results
+
+No positive vmPFC voxel survived whole-brain correction (0 of 6,174 mask voxels). The descriptive mean participant estimate within the mask was −0.0103 (95% t interval −0.0290 to 0.0084; t(53) = −1.10; one-sided p = .862); 21 of 54 participant averages were positive. Leave-one-participant-out ROI means ranged from −0.0144 to −0.0076. These data do not support the predicted positive vmPFC response.
+
+There were 24 positive voxels surviving whole-brain correction elsewhere. The strongest was at MNI [−26, −102, −3.6] mm (mean estimate 0.1121, t = 6.62, max-t FWE p = .0010), outside the vmPFC mask. This finding does not support the vmPFC-specific hypothesis.
+
+![Participant estimates averaged within the vmPFC atlas mask](final-v3/vmpfc-participant-estimates.png)
+
+![Whole-brain corrected peak with vmPFC mask outlined in cyan](final-v3/wholebrain-fwe-map.png)
+
+## Interpretation and limits
+
+This is a lack of corrected evidence for the hypothesized positive vmPFC response, not evidence that the true response is exactly zero or that smaller effects are absent. The ROI interval includes zero and modest positive values. The inference depends on sign-flip exchangeability and approximately symmetric participant errors; the one-sided maximum-t correction is conservative and voxelwise. The vmPFC anatomy is broad and atlas-dependent, though the corrected positive peak is far posterior to this mask.
+
+The inputs are unthresholded AO86 participant contrast parameter estimates, not standardized statistics or group results. Upstream gain regressors were mean-centered and variance-normalized before HRF convolution, so these coefficients cannot be read as change per currency unit. The provided effects come from a gain model separate from the loss model and are conditional on that choice. Because participant variance maps and the executable first-level workflow were not supplied, this analysis cannot use first-level uncertainty for precision-weighted mixed-effects inference; the group test uses between-participant variation in the supplied estimates. No time-series scans or upstream processing were rerun.
+
+All 54 listed participants were included; no maps failed checksum, geometry, or finite-value checks, and no exclusions were made. The common-support rule, input checksums, atlas mask, voxelwise maps, permutation maxima, and machine-readable summary are retained with the outputs.
+
+## Reproduction record
+
+Run from the repository root with `pixi run analysis`. The fixed protocol is [protocol.md](../protocol.md), and the executable analysis is [code/analyze.py](../code/analyze.py). The final validated analysis run used code commit `a33c099ac46cbf769f6510f5ca2149cfdae0af2d`; its exact Pixi lock SHA-256 is recorded in [summary.json](final-v3/summary.json). Complete stdout, stderr, resource samples and duct summaries for the accepted run are in `logs/group-analysis-final-v3-*`; failed attempts and the corrected retries are retained under their own prefixes. Input image retrieval URLs and checksums are in [sources.json](../input/sources.json), and all computed values are in [summary.json](final-v3/summary.json), [participant-vmpfc-effects.tsv](final-v3/participant-vmpfc-effects.tsv), and [input-checksums.tsv](final-v3/input-checksums.tsv).
